Some things you can't forget. But you can fight to make them better.|Tala Durith, to Obi-Wan Kenobi|audio=Tala-PartV-13.50.flac|{{Kenobi|Part V}}}} '''Tala Durith''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|female]] who served in the [[Imperial Army]] in the [[Galactic Empire]]. While on the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] [[Garel]], she participated in the [[Execution of Force-sensitive individuals on Garel|execution]] of four [[Force-sensitive]] families. Having initially joined the Empire to make a positive difference, she was disillusioned by the Empire's cruelty. Afterward, Durith joined the underground network known as the [[Hidden Path]] and began helping smuggle [[The Force|Force]]-sensitive individuals out of the Empire's reach. She and other dissidents, such as the Path's leader, [[Kawlan Roken]], worked with [[Order 66|surviving]] [[Jedi]] and others to operate a network of safehouses that moved people to the Outer Rim planet [[Jabiim]] to receive new identities. At some point, Durith was stationed in a [[Mapuzo mining village|mining village]] on the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim]] planet [[Mapuzo]] as part of the world's Imperial [[Mapuzo battery|battery]]. While [[Spy|maintaining]] her cover as one of the Empire's [[captain]]s, she and the [[loader droid]] [[NED-B]] continued assisting the Hidden Path by operating one of the organization's [[Mapuzo safehouse|safehouses]] and coordinating pickups from the planet. In [[9 BBY]], Durith traveled to rendezvous [[Galactic coordinates|coordinates]] sent to her by the [[con artist]] [[Haja Estree]] with three Imperial [[stormtrooper]]s, whom she [[Death|killed]] upon arrival to [[Battle on Mapuzo|assist]] her new charges, the [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and the [[Alderaanian]] [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]]. After escorting them to the Mapuzo safehouse, Durith attempted to flee the world with Organa while Kenobi stayed behind to distract their pursuer, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]. However, she later left the princess to rescue the Jedi from Imperial capture, successfully extracting him to Jabiim. Organa, meanwhile, was apprehended by the Imperial [[Inquisitor]] [[Reva Sevander|Third Sister]], who had killed the [[Unidentified human pilot (Mapuzo)|pilot]] assisting Durith. Not long after, she and Kenobi mounted a [[Rescue of Princess Leia (9 BBY)|rescue mission]] for Organa with the assistance of the Hidden Path, planning to infiltrate the [[Water|underwater]] [[Fortress Inquisitorius]] on the [[moon]] [[Nur]] in the [[Mustafar system]]. Durith used her [[Imperial officer|officer]] clearance to access the [[fortress]], overriding an entry port to allow the Jedi to sneak inside. When questioned by a [[Unidentified Imperial terminal officer|terminal officer]] and led away from her station, she killed him and continued assisting the Jedi. Durith interrupted the Third [[Sister (Inquisitorius)|Sister's]] planned interrogation of Organa, allowing Kenobi to rescue her from a [[torture]] chamber. She reunited with the pair and met in a [[hangar]], engaging in a brief skirmish with stormtroopers. The pair successfully fled the fortress with Organa, escaping via a Hidden Path [[T-47 airspeeder|airspeeder]] to retreat to Jabiim. Having tracked them to the world, Vader [[Attack on Jabiim|attacked]] the dissidents' [[Jabiim Hidden Path safehouse|base]]. In the attack, Durith was shot in the abdomen by stormtroopers and immobilized. She [[Death|chose]] to detonate a [[thermal detonator]] when [[Imperial Military|Imperial forces]] continued to approach, sacrificing herself to successfully buy her allies more [[time]] to avoid capture. ==Biography== ===Disillusion with the Empire=== {{Quote|The Empire said it was a roundup. People not paying their way, taxes for the cause. They lied. There were four families, all Force-sensitive, and we, we gathered them up. I didn't know who they were. I didn't know what the Inquisitors would do. Fourteen people died, and six of them were children.|Tala Durith, to Obi-Wan Kenobi|audio=Tala-PartV-13.04.flac|}} [[File:TalaDurith-Databank.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Tala Durith served as an Imperial captain.]] Tala Durith [[Homeworld|hailed]] from the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim]] [[mining]] [[planet]] [[Mapuzo]]. Not long after the beginning of the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[Imperial Era|reign]] in [[19 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]'' Durith joined the [[Galaxy|galactic]] [[Politics|government's]] service in the hopes that she could foster positive change throughout [[the galaxy]], eventually becoming an [[Imperial officer]] in the [[Imperial Army]].{{Kenobi|Part IV}} At some point by [[9 BBY]], Durith was [[Execution of Force-sensitive individuals on Garel|deployed]] to the planet''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' [[Garel]] and given orders to round up people that had apparently not [[Currency|paid]] their taxes. The captain complied and assisted [[Imperial Military|Imperial forces]] in gathering fourteen individuals from four [[Force-sensitive]] families—including six [[Youngling|children]]. Horrified,{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|76|Pilots and Crew Members}} the [[officer]] then watched as members of the Empire's [[Jedi hunter|Jedi-hunting]]{{Kenobi|Part II}} [[Inquisitorius]] [[Death|executed]] the families. Following the executions, Durith became disillusioned with the Empire and regretted the mistakes she had made during her deployments, having realized the depth of the atrocities she had abetted while in Imperial service. At some point, Durith carved a marking on her [[Tala Durith's holster|holster]] for each individual that Imperial forces had killed on Garel. Eventually, her committment to helping others led her to discover an underground, anti-Imperial network known as the [[Hidden Path]] and began to work with them. The organization operated several safehouses on worlds across the galaxy to help Jedi and other [[The Force|Force]]-sensitives reach the planet [[Jabiim]] and other safe locations where they could be assigned new identities and live outside the Empire's reach. Durith [[Spy|maintained]] her position as an Imperial officer as a cover, operating officially at a [[Mapuzo battery|battery]] on Mapuzo following her promotion to the [[military rank]] of [[captain]]. While assisting the Path, Durith worked with the Path's leader, [[Kawlan Roken]], who had lost his Force-sensitive [[Kawlan Roken's wife|wife]] to the [[Inquisitor]]s, and also conspired with the Jedi [[Quinlan Vos]], who helped younglings reach safety. She also maintained contact with [[Haja Estree]], a [[con artist]] working on the planet [[Daiyu]] who posed as a Jedi for profit while also helping Force-sensitive [[refugee]]s reach the Path. At some point, Durith began assisting with Path activities on Mapuzo, helped by the [[loader droid]] [[NED-B]] stationed in the organization's [[Mapuzo safehouse|safehouse]] on the world. ===A timely encounter=== {{Quote|We have safehouses like this throughout the galaxy. Trying to link the systems. Some call it the Path. You're not the first Jedi to come through here. It all leads to Jabiim, and from there, we give them new identities and get them out.|Tala Durith, to Obi-Wan Kenobi|audio=Tala-PartIII-25.12.flac|}} [[File:TalaTreason-OWK.png|thumb|right|300px|Tala Durith saved Kenobi and Organa from capture.]] In 9 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]], Estree [[Search for Princess Leia|encountered]] the [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and the [[Alderaanian]] [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] while Inquisitors and [[bounty hunter]]s were [[Hunt for Obi-Wan|chasing]] the pair on Daiyu. The con artist helped Kenobi and Organa reach a [[Transport eight|transport]] to Mapuzo, informing Durith of a pickup arrangement at a set of [[Galactic coordinates|coordinates]]. The officer arranged for a [[Unidentified human pilot (Mapuzo)|pilot]] to transport her new charges offworld later that [[Standard day|day]], giving him an estimate of when she would need his services. She then began making her way to the designated meeting location in an [[CSL-430 hover transport|Imperial ground troop transport]] with three [[stormtrooper]]s. However, the officer was unable to rendezvous with Kenobi and Organa before an Imperial [[Viper probe droid|probe droid]] identified the pair at an Imperial [[Mapuzo checkpoint|checkpoint]]. As the Jedi and the princess fled the area, having [[Battle on Mapuzo|eliminated]] the checkpoint's security, Durith's [[troop transport]] intercepted the two, and the officer's stormtroopers surrounded them. Durith then used her [[blaster]] to shoot the Imperial [[soldier]]s with her, shocking the Jedi and his charge. After explaining that she had been on her way to meet them at Estree's coordinates, Durith led Kenobi and Organa through a nearby [[Mapuzo mining village|mining village]] and into one of the Hidden Path's safehouses. The officer introduced them to NED-B, assuring them that the [[droid]] was on their side. After Durith led them into the safehouse's hidden room, she discussed how she had joined Imperial service and why she no longer believed in the government's [[New Order|ideals]]. As Kenobi studied the room's inscription-covered walls, the officer informed him that many Jedi had been through Path safehouses, including one of his former mission partners, Vos. A pair of stormtroopers entered the Path's safehouse, searching for Kenobi. Although the [[trooper]]s failed to locate the Jedi, Durith contacted her [[pilot]] and ordered him to prepare to leave Mapuzo immediately. She changed out of her [[Imperial officer's uniform|officer's uniform]] and packed a [[backpack]] for the trip ahead. Organa questioned whether it was frightening to need to live a double-life by pretending to be an Imperial, to which the officer replied that it could be, but was nevertheless worth it if she could help people. [[File:DurithKenobiGuardDoor-OWKpIII.png|thumb|left|300px|Durith and Kenobi stand at the ready as stormtroopers enter the safehouse.]] When asked by Kenobi, Durith explained that she risked rebelling against the Empire through her Path work to assuage the guilt of her past actions as an Imperial officer. As the trio prepared to flee through a tunnel connected to the safehouse, Kenobi sensed the arrival of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] on Mapuzo. She and the Jedi watched Vader venture further into the mining village from their safehouse's [[Viewport|window]] for a moment before eventually pulling away. Kenobi implored Durith to flee with Organa, making the officer promise to return the child to her homeworld, the [[Core Worlds]] planet Alderaan. As they fled, Kenobi exited the safehouse and ran further from Durith and Organa, hoping to give them [[time]] to escape. ===Rescue from Vader=== {{Quote|Keep running till you reach the port. A pilot will meet you there.|Tala Durith, to Leia Organa|audio=Tala-PartIII-35.56.flac|}} [[File:LeiaHugsTala-OWKpIII.png|thumb|right|275px|Durith and Organa hugged before parting ways.]] As the pair ran down an escape tunnel, Organa begged Durith to go back and assist Kenobi. Though the officer initially refused, she eventually decided to help the Jedi and instructed the princess to keep running to the end of the path until she met their escape pilot at a nearby [[Mapuzo port|port]]. Durith then ran the way she had come, returning to the safehouse to meet with NED-B. As Imperial forces circled an injured Kenobi, she and NED-B drew closer to the Jedi's location and surveyed Kenobi and Vader's confrontation from a nearby cliffside. The officer fired blaster shots at Vader's forces from above and ignited a pile of [[Fire|flammable]] stones, causing them to break formation. In the chaos, NED-B carried Kenobi away from the scene and to a secluded area. As Durith inspected Kenobi's injuries, she asked the loader droid to prepare their [[Tala Durith's shuttle|shuttle]] for immediate departure to Jabiim. She, NED-B, and the Jedi swiftly departed Mapuzo aboard the [[Starship|vessel]]. However, the Imperial Inquisitor [[Reva Sevander|Third Sister]] killed the pilot Organa had been sent to meet and captured the princess. As Kenobi drifted in and out of consciousness, she assured him he would be alright. After landing on Jabiim, Durith escorted the injured Kenobi's stretcher through a [[Jabiim Hidden Path safehouse|Hidden Path safehouse]] and watched over him as he healed in a [[bacta tank]]. Kenobi jolted awake while recovering in the tank and pulled himself out of it, despite the officer's protests that he was still injured. He and Durith then went to find Roken, who was displeased with the risk the Jedi's presence at the base posed. Kenobi implored Roken to help rescue Organa, and Durith supported him, mentioning that the princess knew about the Path's activities on Jabiim and could expose their operations if pressured. [[File:KenobiDurithPlanRaid-OWKpIV.png|thumb|left|300px|Durith and Kenobi discuss the raid on Fortress Inquisitorius.]] Roken reluctantly agreed to assist them, leading the pair to one of the Path's control rooms, which housed a [[Hologram|holographic]] depiction of the [[moon]] [[Nur]]—home to the [[Water|underwater]] [[Fortress Inquisitorius]]. Durith promised to infiltrate the facility with Kenobi, despite the misgivings of other her other colleagues, [[Sully Stark]] and [[Wade Resselian]]. Although they were unsure that her cover as an Imperial officer was intact, Durith felt it was worth trying to use it as an advantage to infiltrate the [[fortress]]. In preparation for their mission, she had her ship [[Fuel|refueled]] and donned her officer's [[Clothing|uniform]] as a disguise. As she and Kenobi traveled to the [[Mustafar system]], the officer encouraged him to take time to heal and forget the past. ===Fortress rescue=== {{Quote|God, look at this place. What are they keeping down there?''"
"''Where is ''[Leia Organa]''?''"
"''Detention area's in a secure sector. Just keep heading north.|Tala Durith and Obi-Wan Kenobi|audio=TalaandKenobi-PartIV-14.07.flac|}} Upon landing in the fortress's [[hangar]], Durith confidently strode past Imperial personnel to an entrance checkpoint. When questioned by the Imperial [[security guard]] [[Tytan Latimer]], the captain insisted she had clearance and submitted her [[Code cylinder|cylinder]] to him. Despite the terminal officer's initial refusal to let her pass, they eventually permitted her entry after she threatened to report them to [[the Grand Inquisitor]] for not letting her through to deliver classified intelligence. Once inside, Durith sat at a terminal and used her [[comlink]] to contact Kenobi. She guided him toward a port that she had overridden, and he entered the facility. [[File:RevaDoesntBelieveInPersonalSpace-OWKpIV.png|thumb|right|300px|The Third Sister accused Durith of treason.]] When Durith was confronted at her station by a [[Unidentified Imperial terminal officer|terminal officer]], they escorted her out to verify her identity. She quickly killed the officer, later reassuring Kenobi that she had encountered some company and eliminated the threat. After being told by the Jedi to cause a distraction, Durith rushed to Organa's interrogation chamber and requested an audience with Third [[Sister (Inquisitorius)|Sister]], the Inquisitor who had been preparing to [[torture]] the princess. When granted an audience, Durith expounded on a falsified story to buy time, claiming that Hidden Path insurgents were hiding Kenobi on the planet [[Florrum]] using a salvage business as a front. However, Third Sister instead ordered that she be apprehended, having sensed that she was lying. Though troopers detained her, the captain swiftly took them down with a blaster and reunited with the Jedi and Organa, who had just exited the torture chamber. As Durith and the princess ran down a corridor, Kenobi held back a cracking window, letting water spill in and flood the area after the trio had escaped behind a door. As Durith entered the hangar, she walked alongside Kenobi, who was hiding Organa under an Imperial [[greatcoat]]. The fortress was locked down, resulting in the trio's capture by nearby troopers. When Third Sister denounced Durith as an Imperial [[Treason|traitor]], she responded that she never was loyal in the first place. The Inquisitor ordered the trio's execution, but before troopers could carry out the order, Stark and Resselian's [[T-47 airspeeder]]s strafed the Imperials in the hangar. Kenobi, Organa, and Durith fled amidst the chaos, gunning down everything in their path. Though the trio successfully escaped on Stark's [[airspeeder]], they were saddened when Imperials downed Ressellian's vessel in the ensuing chaos. After Stark's [[Speeder|airspeeder]] transferred them to a larger ship, Durith briefly reminisced about their fallen comrade's sacrifice. Once the vessel landed at the Path's Jabiim base, Durith disembarked. ===Attack on Jabiim=== {{Quote|If you surrender, she died for nothing. He'll keep coming.''"
"''That's why I have to stop him.|Kawlan Roken and Obi-Wan Kenobi after Tala Durith's death|audio=KawlanandKenobi-PartV-23.01.flac|}} Shortly afterward, Vader's [[Devastator|Star Destroyer]] [[Attack on Jabiim|arrived]] on Jabiim, and he issued orders to lock down the Path's base as the [[Saboteur|sabotage]] of Organa's [[Toy droid|droid]], [[L0-LA59]], had locked their hangar doors. Durith and Kenobi briefly discussed the situation and speculated on Vader's next plans. While the Jedi Master prepared to confront Vader, Durith began helping Roken determine how to re-open the hangar. She later found Kenobi elsewhere in the base, confiding that she had participated in a massacre of Force-sensitive families on Garel while working as an Imperial officer and now chose to fight against the Empire's cruelty to assuage her guilt. As Imperial forces drew closer to the base's entrance, Durith joined the ranks of the Path's fighters while Kenobi attempted to stall for time by initiating a conversation with Third Sister. [[File:TalaDurithSacrifice-OWKpV.png|thumb|left|300px|Durith sacrificed herself to allow her compatriots to escape.]] When the stalling attempt failed, the Third Sister's troopers breached the Path base. Durith and her colleagues began shooting at the intruders, but the Imperials vastly outnumbered them. As she retreated with the others deeper into the base, Durith was hit in the abdomen with blaster fire and fell to the ground. Kenobi and NED-B attempted to rescue her, with the latter carrying the woman and using his body as a shield. However, she implored Kenobi to retreat, [[Death|activating]] a [[thermal detonator]] after shooting the blast door control between them. The Jedi grieved Durith's sacrifice and wanted to surrender, but Roken dissuaded him. Eventually, Organa managed to reopen the hangar doors, allowing the Path's members to escape aboard a [[JT-731 Broadhorn transport|ship]]. Having held on to Durith's blaster [[holster]], Kenobi gave it to the princess when they left Jabiim. When she later asked why the holster did not come with a blaster, the Jedi said he would not bequeath a ten-[[Standard year|year]]-old child a blaster. Organa kept Tala's holster with her after returning to Alderaan and used it as a place to keep her droid L0-LA.{{Kenobi|Part VI}} ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Why do you do this? Risk everything?''"
"''I joined up when the Empire stood for something. By the time I realized what they really were, it was too late. I made some mistakes.|Obi-Wan Kenobi and Tala Durith|audio=TalaandKenobi-PartIII-28.32.flac|}} [[File:DurithTheDefender-OWKpV.png|thumb|right|270px|Durith fought against Imperials on Jabiim.]] Durith was an idealistic woman who became disillusioned with the Galactic Empire after witnessing its violence towards civilians and children. In particular, she felt that the ideal galaxy she wished to live in could not coexist with a regime as oppressive of the Empire. Durith involved herself in the activities of the Path in order to atone for her role in a massacre on Garel, and felt sympathetic for those who were mistreated by the Empire, including Force-sensitives and droids. On Jabiim, Durith was willing to sacrifice herself to buy her allies more time to escape, blowing herself up with a [[Grenade|detonator]]. The woman found purpose in her work helping the individuals that Imperials sought to destroy, having developed deep loyalty to the rebels she worked with. The officer's dogged pursuit of the Path's goals led her to display a certain degree of ruthlessness, as exemplified by her willingness to murder troops under her own command to save Force-sensitive refugees from execution. While on Mapuzo, Durith built a friendly rapport with Organa, showing her why she wore her holster on a particular side, though not showing the girl how to shoot despite the latter's request. While in Fortress Inquisitorius, she was willing to lie to achieve her goals, readily killing Imperials who posed a threat to her and Kenobi's rescue of Organa. A human female, she had [[Color|brown]] [[eye]]s and tan skin. While serving as an Imperial officer, Durith kept her raven-black [[hair]] styled in a bun fastened with pins under her [[Imperial kepi|uniform kepi]]. ==Skills and abilities== {{Quote|…I have officer clearance. I can get you inside, and I can get you access.|Tala Durith, to Obi-Wan Kenobi while planning a rescue|audio=Tala-PartIV-7.06.flac|}} Durith was skilled with a blaster, accurately firing [[blaster pistol]]s and [[Blaster rifle|rifles]] from both short and long range. The officer was also trained in [[Unarmed combat|hand-to-hand combat]], being able to silently dispatch an opponent larger than herself within [[second]]s. While working for the Path, Durith regularly engaged in subterfuge. She confidently lied while maintaining her cover as an Imperial officer, weaving elaborate justifications for her duplicitous behavior whenever questioned. ==Equipment== {{Quote|I wear it on the other side. Gives me a faster draw.|Tala Durith to Leia Organa about her holster|audio=Tala-PartIII-28.15.flac|}} [[File:TalaDurithImpUniform-SWCT.png|thumb|left|190px|Tala Durith wearing her Imperial officer's uniform]] While stationed on Mapuzo, Durith donned a gray-green Imperial officer's uniform, including an Imperial [[Hat|kepi]] bearing an [[officer's disk]], code cylinder, black [[glove]]s, and black [[leather]] [[boot]]s. She also wore brown [[belt]] with a silver buckle that also had an officer's disk. She displayed the [[rank insignia plaque]] of an Imperial Army captain, on the [[breast]] of her uniform, composed of a single row of three red squares and one blue. Durith carried a [[SE-14r light repeating blaster]] with her while on Mapuzo, which she kept in a holster by her hip. On Jabiim, she wielded a [[WE-11 blaster pistol]]. After the Garel executions, Durith carved a marking into her holster for each individual that had died during the event. While on Mapuzo, Durith wore a long-sleeved light blue shirt under her officer's uniform. She paired the shirt with a ribbed brown tunic and a multicolored, patterned sash. In preparation to leave the world, she fastened a brown holster belt to her waist and took a brown backpack with her from the Path safehouse. She also possessed an [[Iota-class TS-485 light shuttle|''Iota''-class TS-485 light shuttle]], which she used to assist Kenobi in saving Organa. The shuttle was ideal for Durith's operations as a rebel spy, being both compact and able to be piloted by a single operator.{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|76|History of the Ship}} While rescuing Organa from the Inquisitors' fortress, Durith used a comlink to communicate with Kenobi. On Jabiim, the she activated a thermal detonator in her dying moments to give her allies more time to escape. After Durith's death, Kenobi bequeathed Durith's holster to Organa as a memento. ==Behind the scenes== ===Milestones=== {{Quote|I feel like this is a really exciting time to sort of change the landscape of the way women are perceived. And it's really exciting to have a female director leading this and trusting that it will be… We will be represented in the right way, because ''[Deborah Chow is]'' on it.|Indira Varma discussing her role as Tala Durith|{{WebCite|url=https://www.elle.com/culture/movies-tv/a40151808/who-is-tala-obi-wan-kenobi-indira-varma-star-wars|text=Indira Varma On Her ''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' Character Reveal: "Tala Has A Lovely Arc"|author=[https://www.elle.com/author/429567/lauren-puckett-pope Puckett-Pope, Lauren]|date=2022-06-01|work=[[Wikipedia:Elle (magazine)|ELLE.com]]|archivedate=20220606034947}}}} [[File:TalaDurith-OWKPoster.png|thumb|right|230px|Tala Durith debuted in ''Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi''.]] Tala Durith was first pictured in the teaser trailer for the [[Disney+]] television series ''[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'', which was released on [[March 9]], [[2022]].{{SWYouTube|TWTfhyvzTx0|Obi-Wan Kenobi | Teaser Trailer | Disney+|sw_url=video/teaser-trailer-obi-wan-kenobi}} She first appeared in the [[Part III|third episode]] of the series, which aired on [[June 1]] of that year.{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-june-2022|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in June 2022}} She was portrayed by actress [[Indira Varma]]. Her Imperial rank and full name were revealed on a [[viewscreen]] in [[aurebesh]] in the [[Part IV|fourth episode]] of the series. While Varma's involvement in Kenobi was officially revealed in ''Obi-Wan Kenobi''{{'s}} casting announcement on [[March 29]], [[2021]],{{SW|url=news/obi-wan-kenobi-series-cast|text=''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' Series to Begin Production in April, Cast Revealed}} an exclusive by [[Wikipedia:Deadline (magazine)|Deadline]] leaked her that she had joined the cast on [[March 1]] of that year.{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2021/03/obi-wan-kenobi-series-star-wars-game-of-thrones-indira-varma-disney-plus-1234704207|text=Obi-Wan Kenobi Series: 'Game Of Thrones' & 'For Life' Star Indira Varma Set To Join Disney+ 'Star Wars' Spinoff|author=[https://deadline.com/author/andreas-wiseman Wiseman, Andreas]|date=2021-03-01|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline (magazine)|Deadline]]|archivedate=20220609145028}} For the month of [[November]] [[2024]], Durith was the Character of the Month on the mobile game ''[[Star Wars: Card Trader]]''.{{Twitter|ToppsSWCT|status/1859280645941281096|name=Star Wars™: Card Trader by Topps®|date=2024-11-20|quote=Tala Durith is SWCT's November Character of the Month! Post your all-time favorite Tala Durith pull from SWCT + your in-app username & #SWCTSpotlight for a chance to win crystals tomorrow!|archivefile=File:TalaDurithSWCT.png}} Durith received a ''[[Star Wars: The Black Series]]'' action figure,{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Black Series|packtype=''Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi'' Figure|pack=#13: Tala Durith (Imperial Officer)|link=products/star-wars-the-black-series-tala-imperial-officer}} which was sculpted by [[Sarah Lynn Reynolds]] in [[Wikipedia:ZBrush|ZBrush]]. Reynolds particularly enjoyed Durith as a character, having sculpted all parts of the figure except for the blaster, which was pulled from other, pre-existing figures as the sculptor felt it looked better.{{ArtStation|username=bearrrs|url=artwork/WmW5g3|name=[[Sarah Lynn Reynolds]]|text=Hasbro Star Wars Black Series Tala|archivefile=File:TalaDurith-SarahLynnReynoldsArtstation.png}} Two cards featuring Durith were included in the [[Secrets of Power]] set of [[Fantasy Flight Games]]' [[Star Wars: Unlimited|''Star Wars'': Unlimited]] card game,{{SWU|set=Secrets of Power|cardname=Tala Durith|subtitle=I Can Get You Inside|type=Hyperspace|link=4621667816}}{{SWU|set=Secrets of Power|cardname=Tala Durith|subtitle=I Can Get You Inside|type=Prestige|link=8698847723}} released on [[November 7]], [[2025]].{{UnlimitedWeb|url=products/set-6-secrets-of-power|text=Set 6 Secrets of Power}} [[Tyler Parrott]], the set's head designer,{{YouTube|video=FbA5ZtoUegE|text=STAR WARS: Unlimited Designer Insight | Fantasy Flight Games|channel=FantastFlightGames1|name=Fantasy Flight Games}} described the role of Durith's role in the card set as "cheap leader protection," to protect the player's main leader by taking on attacks.{{Bluesky|username=davflamerock.bsky.social|url=post/3m2jy2zlgy22t|name=[[Tyler Parrott]]|date=2025-10-06|quote=We wanted all our Plots to fill different niches for what you might want to do with your leader, one of which is "protect the leader." Tala's role, therefore, is to be cheap leader protection…even if it means she takes the attack in place of your leader #FFGStaff|archivedate=20251029184026}} ===Recruitment=== {{Quote|And even though I don't come from a place of being a massive fan, and I haven't watched it throughout its entire 45 years, I visited it over the years, and I thought, 'Well, I'm going to have to do a little bit of research here.' I knew it was Deborah Chow directing, so I wanted to watch ''The Mandalorian'', and also because it had ''[''Game of Thrones'' costar Pedro Pascal]'' in there.|Indira Varma on researching for her role|{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/tv/obi-wan-kenobi-indira-varma-love-interest|text=Indira Varma reveals Tala was originally conceived as a love interest for Obi-Wan Kenobi|author=[https://ew.com/author/dalton-ross Ross, Dalton]|date=2022-06-02|work=[[Entertainment Weekly Books|''Entertainment Weekly'']]|archivedate=20220620172002}}}} [[File:Indira-Nur-filming.png|thumb|left|300px|Indira Varma on set as Durith]] According to Varma, she first took interest in joining the cast of ''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' when her manager brought up the opening of a role in the series. By the time she had been cast as Durith, Varma had not watched any of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' franchise and felt that she did not need an encyclopedic knowledge of ''Star Wars'' to understand her character's motivations. Nevertheless, Varma chose to research the franchise by watching the Disney+{{SW|url=news/pedro-pascal-revealed-as-the-mandalorian|text=Pedro Pascal Revealed as ''The Mandalorian''}} television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', as ''Obi-Wan Kenobi''{{'s}} director [[Deborah Chow]] had been part of it and her friend [[Pedro Pascal]], a co-star of hers in the fantasy franchise [[Wikipedia:Game of Thrones|''Game of Thrones'']], was the lead character. Having enjoyed the wit, humanity, and serialized feel of ''The Mandalorian'', Varma conversed with Chow and they talked about joining the show. Varma trusted Chow's sensibilities and liked how the director wanted the show to be character driven and Chow asked for her input. Varma saw being in the show was an exciting time to change how women are perceived and found her character unique. That made her feel more welcome in ''Star Wars'', which in the past she had considered a boys' franchise, and she believed she didn't need to copy any other portrayal as she was not reprising an existing character. ===Production=== {{Quote|The holster was a challenge ''[…]'' it had to both hold Leia's droid as well as the blaster we designed for Tala. For Leia, we took the drop portion off of the gun belt and it just so happened to fit her nearly perfectly. It was a super tricky puzzle to solve, but so satisfying when it actually worked.|Propmaster [[Brad Elliot]], on Durith's holster|{{SW|url=news/inside-the-lucasfilm-archive-obi-wan-kenobi-props-3|text=Inside the Lucasfilm Archive: A Brewing Rebellion in the ''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' Limited Series}}}} [[File:Guns-on-camera.png|thumb|right|300px|Durith's blaster was modified so her holster's fit could take L0-LA as well.]] By the time Varma learned about Durith, her character's story had gone through a number of incarnations. According to the actress, Durith reportedly originated as a love interest for Obi-Wan Kenobi, but Chow and showwriter [[Joby Harold]] ultimately dropped that idea, feeling that it was too [[Wikipedia:Cliché|cliché]]. Durith's holster was made to fit both her and its inheritor Leia Organa. The designers removed the drop portion from the gun belt to fit Organa well. In order to be a fit for both Durith's blaster and eventually Organa's droid L0-LA, the blaster was designed with a scope in the style of [[Han's heavy blaster pistol|Han Solo's blaster]] that could require a holster space that fitted the droid as well. The detonator which Durith used to sacrifice herself was inspired by the one used by Leia Organa in the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]'' [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] and was made from a replica that was modified by the designers. On her first day of filming, Varma was amused by the presence of stormtroopers and was exhilarated when she first saw [[Darth]] Vader on set. According to Varma, she worked well with Kenobi's actor [[Ewan McGregor]], who playfully teased her on multiple occasions for having not seen the ''Star Wars'' films. At the end of filming for the sequence''[[Obi-Wan Kenobi: A Jedi's Return]]'' where Durith perishes in the episode "[[Part V]]," which released on [[June 15]], 2022,{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-june-2022|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in June 2022}} the actor called it an emotional day. Varma enjoyed filming in "[[Wikipedia:StageCraft|the Volume]]," a 360-degrees [[Wikipedia:Light-emitting diode|LED]] screen set that projected the background around her. The actor's trainer named Lacey introduced her to ice baths, which she gained a habit of doing.{{WebCite|url=https://www.vogue.com/article/obi-wan-kenobi-indira-varma-interview|text=''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' Star Indira Varma Is Over Being Typecast|author=[https://www.vogue.com/contributor/arushi-sinha Sinha, Arushi]|date=2022-06-02|work=[[Wikipedia:Vogue|Vogue]]|archivedate=20220610061913}} Though Durith's transport is a variant of [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|standard Imperial shuttles]], the art department for ''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' decided to create a new model rather than using a pre-existing design. The new model was made to have several visual similarities to vessels seen in other ''Star Wars'' works, such as ''Return of the Jedi''. For ''Obi-Wan Kenobi'', the shuttle was visualized by [[Industrial Light & Magic]]'s StageCraft Volume, as its 360 degree LED screen was able to project it for the set. ===Characterization=== {{Quote|I play Tala and she's actually the equivalent of the French resistance. She has been hurt. Deeply, deeply disillusioned by the Empire and has since switched her allegiance. I think she sees Ben. She understands him. She sees a man who's given up. Who's lost his mojo. And she tries to galvanize him to face his past, and to face his fears.|Varma describes Durith's role in ''Obi-Wan Kenobi''|}} [[File:IndiraVarmaNED-B.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Indira Varma in costume as Tala Durith with NED-B]] McGregor considered the character of Tala Durith to be important for encouraging Kenobi to leave the past in the past and leave his past behind. Varma similarly saw the character as someone who wanted to help Kenobi face his past and fears. She considered Durith to be someone who had been hurt and deeply disillusioned with the Empire. Durith's character was based on the [[Wikipedia:French Resistance|French Resistance]], which opposed the [[Wikipedia:German military administration in occupied France during World War II|Nazi occupation]] of [[Wikipedia:France|France]]{{WebCite|url=https://www.historytoday.com/archive/review/french-resistance-olivier-wieviorka-review|text='The French Resistance' by Olivier Wieviorka review|author=[https://www.historytoday.com/author/martin-evans Evans, Martin]|date=2018-08-08|work=[[Wikipedia:History Today|History Today]]|archivedate=20230923201310}} during the [[Wikipedia:World War II|Second World War]], Varma similarly felt that her character resembled the organization, noting in an interview that she sees Kenobi as a man who has given up, but tries to galvanize him to face his past. Varma felt that while Durith was not romantically involved with Kenobi, she was still willing to give up everything to further his quest. The actor considered Durith's character a risk-it-all type who had nothing to lose as she attempted to atone for her past sins.{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/obi-wan-kenobi-indira-varma-imperial-officer-character-1235153889|text='Obi-Wan Kenobi' Actress Indira Varma Explores "Disillusioned" Imperial Officer Character and Talks Prior Franchise Dissatisfaction|author=[https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/author/ryan-parker-thr Parker, Ryan]|date=2022-06-01|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20220808184317}} Varma and many of her colleagues did not see the final episodes until Kenobi's premiere at [[Celebration Anaheim (2022)|Celebration Anaheim]], nearly a year since they were all working together on ''Obi-Wan Kenobi''.{{YouTube|video=nCPGnhbq2-4|text=INDIRA VARMA Interview Star Wars Celebration Obi-Wan Kenobi Event|channel=@StageRightSecrets|name=StageRightSecrets|date=2022-05-28}} The composer [[Natalie Holt]], who worked on ''Obi-Wan Kenobi'', used a [[Wikipedia:Nyckelharpa|nyckelharpa]] instrument for some of the scenes in the Mapuzo safehouse.
